entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of both sides.

2. This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, challenging the judgment and award dated 03.12.2014 passed in MVC No.762/2008, by the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, D.K. Mangalore, C/C (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, D.K. Mangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. One Anil Tauro, met with an accident on 26.11.2006 and died subsequently.
His elder brothers and sisters, who are unmarried filed a claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.16,00,000/-.

The Tribunal, after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,45,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
4. Aggrieved by the said award, the present appeal is preferred.
It is contended that the deceased-Anil NC: 2026:KHC:6990 HC-KAR Tauro was aged 38 years, working as a cloth merchant and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Appellant Nos.1 and 4, who are the unmarried sisters of the deceased, were dependent on his income.

The Tribunal, however, observed that all the claimants were majors, and they were not dependants and consequently declined to award compensation towards 'loss of dependency', while also deducting 50% towards personal expenses.
The Tribunal further failed to consider 'future prospects' and did not award any compensation under the heads of 'loss of estate' and 'loss of love and affection'.
The Tribunal only granted Rs.10,000/- towards 'funeral expenses', Rs.3,10,000/- towards 'medical expenses' as incurred and Rs.25,000/- towards 'food and conveyance etc. during treatment period'.
Hence, the appellants seeks enhancement of the compensation.

5. The learned counsel of the respondent relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.7805/2022 (New Insurance Company and NC: 2026:KHC:6990 HC-KAR Anand Pal and others), contending that siblings are not dependents and therefore not entitled to any compensation.
In the said judgment, it was observed that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary,
brothers and sisters cannot be treated as dependants, as they are ordinarily independent and earning, married or dependent upon their parents.

6. Per contra, learned counsel of the appellant also relied upon the decision reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 554, Sadhana Thomas and Others Vs. Ashok Kushwaha and Others, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the term "legal representative" has a wider interpretation and calls for a liberal interpretation so as to fulfil the legislative intent.

entities.text: Sadhana Thomas and Others Vs. Ashok Kushwaha and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that it is sufficient for a claimant to establish 'loss of dependency' and that a legal representative is one who suffers on account of the death of a person in a motor vehicle accident and therefore, must have a remedy for the realization of compensation.
In the said case, it was held that the father NC: 2026:KHC:6990 HC-KAR and the younger sister of the deceased were not financially independent and were dependent on his income.

In the present case, the deceased-Anil Tauro's parents are no more and the only claimants are his elder brothers aged 53 and 51 years, arrayed as appellant Nos.2 and 3 and his elder sisters aged 43 and 45 years, arrayed as appellant Nos.1 and 4.

The appellants have stated both in their cross-examination and in the grounds of appeal, that they are unmarried and were dependant on the Violet Tauro vs The National Insurance Co. Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52838020/

sentences.text: 7. It is not in dispute that the parents of the deceased are no more.
Learned counsel for the respondent contended that the burden lies upon the claimants to establish loss of dependency and to prove that they were financially dependent on the income of the deceased.

In the present case,
two other brothers of the deceased are alive and there is no cogent evidence on record to establish that the sisters aged 43 and 45 years, were NC: 2026:KHC:6990 HC-KAR unmarried and financially dependent on the income of the deceased at the time of the accident.
8. Learned counsel of the appellants submitted that in the cross-examination it has been specifically stated that both the sisters are unmarried despite being aged 43 and 45 years.
It is therefore contended that they were dependent on the income of the deceased.

In support of the same, the appellants have produced the Legal Heir Certificate-Ex.P-12 issued by the Deputy Tahsildar,
wherein both the sisters are shown as unmarried.
9. It is stated that the deceased-Anil Tauro was aged 38 years at the time of the accident and working as a cloth merchant and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
10. The Tribunal observed that though the deceased had produced a licence valid from 14.08.1998 to 31.03.1999, the accident occurred in the year 2006 and no documentary proof of income was produced.

Therefore, considering that the accident took place in the year 2006, NC:
2026:KHC:6990 HC-KAR notional income of the deceased was taken as Rs.3,500/- per month, as per chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

The deceased being aged 38 years at the time of the accident, the applicable multiplier is '15'.
11.
The deceased is entitled to an additional of 40% towards 'future prospects'.
The notional income assessed at Rs.3,500/- per month, on addition of 40% (Rs.1,400/-) comes to Rs.4,900/- per month.
After deducting 50% towards personal expenses, the monthly contribution to the family would be Rs.2,450/-.
Applying the multiplier of '15', the loss of dependency works out to Rs.4,900/- x 12 x 15 = Rs.8,82,000/-.
Less 50% towards personal expenses = Rs.4,41,000/-.
Therefore, the 'loss of dependency works out to Rs.4,41,000/-.

12. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.3,10,000/- towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.25,000/-
towards 'funeral' Rs.10,000/- towards 'other expenses'.

This Court finds it just and reasonable to confirm the amounts granted by the Tribunal.

13. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different heads (Rs.)
 Future Prospects 4,41,000/-
 Medical expenses 3,10,000/-
 Food, conveyance etc., 25,000/-

- 10 -  NC: 2026:KHC:6990 HC-KAR  ORDER  i. Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The judgment and award dated 03.12.2014 passed in MVC No.762/2008, by the IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, D.K.
